messages.content: I need to put together the Minneapolis trip for my niece's graduation. The ceremony is Sunday afternoon, and my wife and I would leave Atlanta Friday after work and come back Monday. I want to see complete flight-and-hotel combinations, not just separate lists.
What are the dates, and where are the Sunday ceremony and Saturday family dinner? Those locations will make a meaningful difference in the hotel comparison.

Friday, May 15 through Monday, May 18. Graduation is at Northrop at the University of Minnesota at 2:00 Sunday. Dinner is Saturday at 6:30 at my sister's house in Edina, near 50th and France. Two round-trip tickets and one room for three nights.
Thanks. For Friday, what is the earliest time you can leave Atlanta, and on Monday do you need to be home by a particular hour?
We can be at ATL by 5:15 Friday. Monday is open, though I would rather not turn it into a very late night. Nonstop would be helpful, but show me a reasonable connection if it saves enough.

I found two workable flight pairings. Option 1 is Delta nonstop both ways: depart ATL Friday at 7:20 p.m., arrive MSP at 8:58 p.m.; return Monday at 12:15 p.m., arrive ATL at 3:43 p.m. The current total for two in Main Cabin is $876. Option 2 uses Southwest outbound with one stop in St. Louis, leaving at 6:25 p.m. and reaching MSP at 10:20 p.m., then Delta nonstop Monday at 6:05 p.m., arriving Atlanta at 9:31 p.m. Purchased as separate tickets, the current total for two is $704. The connection saves $172 but adds about two hours Friday and creates separate-ticket terms.
The Friday connection is probably too much after work. Is there another nonstop return later Monday so we do not have to leave the hotel first thing?

Yes. Keeping the Friday 7:20 p.m. Delta nonstop, there is a Monday 4:35 p.m. Delta nonstop arriving ATL at 8:02 p.m. That pairing is $932 for two. There is also a 6:05 p.m. return arriving at 9:31 p.m.; paired with the same outbound, it is $904 for two.
Use the 4:35 return in the main comparison. What hotels make sense near the university versus near my sister? I do not want to overlook how long either event takes to reach.

Near Northrop, Graduate by Hilton Minneapolis has a king room for $642 total for three nights, including taxes. It is about a 12-minute walk to Northrop. Driving to the Edina dinner is roughly 20-30 minutes in normal Saturday traffic, with some additional time to park near 50th and France. From MSP, the hotel is about 20 minutes by car or roughly 35 minutes by light rail plus walking. Parking is $30 per night if you rent a car.
And the Edina side?

Homewood Suites by Hilton Edina has a king studio for $573 total, including taxes, with breakfast included. It is about 8-12 minutes by car from the dinner address. Northrop is usually 20-30 minutes by car on Sunday, but you should allow 35 minutes plus parking because graduation traffic can build around campus. MSP is about 15 minutes away by car. Hotel parking is currently complimentary.
We are not planning to rent a car. Please calculate this around rideshares, and include getting to dinner, the ceremony, and the airport.

Using current typical rideshare ranges rather than surge pricing: from Graduate Minneapolis, MSP pickup Friday is about $25, the round trip to Edina Saturday about $70 total, and the Monday airport ride about $25. You can walk to Northrop Sunday, so estimated local transport is $120. From Homewood Suites Edina, airport pickup is about $24, the Saturday dinner round trip about $26, Sunday rides to and from Northrop about $62, and Monday airport transport about $24, totaling about $136.
That is closer than I expected. Does the university hotel leave us stuck for food Friday night if we arrive around nine?

Not entirely, but choices narrow after check-in. Several casual places around Stadium Village serve until 10:00 or 11:00 p.m., and delivery is available. Graduate also has an on-site restaurant, but its kitchen hours should be verified for that Friday. Homewood Suites is quieter late at night; you would likely need delivery or a rideshare to a restaurant after a 9:00 p.m. airport arrival.
Compare the complete totals with the nonstop flights. Also tell me what time we should leave each hotel for Saturday dinner and Sunday graduation.

Package A, university area: Delta nonstop round trip for two at $932, Graduate king room at $642, and estimated rideshares of $120, for an estimated trip total of $1,694. I would leave for Edina at 5:45 p.m. Saturday to allow for traffic and finding the house. On Sunday, leave the hotel on foot around 1:15 p.m. for Northrop, earlier if you want time to meet family before seating. Package B, Edina: the same $932 flights, Homewood Suites king studio at $573, and estimated rideshares of $136, for an estimated total of $1,641. Leave for dinner around 6:00 p.m. Saturday. For graduation, request the ride by 12:50 p.m. Sunday and aim to be dropped off by 1:25.
So Edina is only $53 less after transportation. What are the cancellation terms and room differences?

Graduate's quoted king room is a standard room and can be canceled without penalty until 11:59 p.m. local hotel time on May 13; after that, the first night plus tax is charged. Homewood's king studio has a kitchenette and sofa bed, and cancellation is free until 11:59 p.m. local time on May 14; a late cancellation is charged one night plus tax. Both quotes are for two adults and one room for May 15-18.
Is there any reason to choose the cheaper connecting flight now that we have the hotel totals?

It would reduce either package by $228 compared with the selected $932 nonstop pairing, but it is a weaker fit for this schedule. You would leave Atlanta only 70 minutes after your stated airport arrival time, connect after a workday, reach Minneapolis about 80 minutes later, and return much later Monday. It also splits the itinerary across Southwest and Delta. The savings are real, but the nonstop pairing gives you more margin Friday and a substantially earlier arrival home Monday.
Agreed. Give me the two clean options to send my wife, with the university one first. Do not reserve anything yet.

Option 1, university area: Delta nonstop ATL-MSP Friday, May 15, departing 7:20 p.m. and arriving 8:58 p.m.; Delta nonstop MSP-ATL Monday, May 18, departing 4:35 p.m. and arriving 8:02 p.m. Two Main Cabin tickets are currently $932. Graduate by Hilton Minneapolis is $642 total for one king room for three nights, cancelable through 11:59 p.m. May 13. Estimated rideshares are $120. Estimated trip total: $1,694. The hotel is about a 12-minute walk from Sunday's ceremony; leave at 1:15 p.m. For Saturday dinner in Edina, leave around 5:45 p.m. Option 2, Edina area: the same nonstop flights at $932. Homewood Suites Edina is $573 total for a king studio with kitchenette and breakfast, cancelable through 11:59 p.m. May 14. Estimated rideshares are $136. Estimated trip total: $1,641. Leave around 6:00 p.m. for Saturday dinner and request the Sunday graduation ride by 12:50 p.m. The university option costs about $53 more but makes the central Sunday commitment walkable. Fares, room inventory, and rideshare prices can change. Nothing has been held or purchased.
